domain_setting: A friendly neighborhood café and restaurant with warm wood tables, ceramic plates, folded napkins, menu boards without readable text, kitchen tools, and food being prepared. Keep spaces and roles distinct from the meal and action cards.
recurring_scale_anchors: 304x192 card with essential subject inside x=24..280 and y=16..176
Use café/restaurant furniture only when it clarifies the word; set kitchen methods on a simple counter or stovetop
Food places, menu courses, preparation actions, cooking methods, and ordering/payment should use separate strong silhouettes
No readable labels, words, prices, numbers, logos, or text on menus or bills

polysemy_resolution_table.bar (pub): A public house/bar venue with counter and taps from the Places group, not a rod or metal bar.
polysemy_resolution_table.buffet: A self-service spread of dishes in the Meals group, not a punch or blow.
polysemy_resolution_table.entrée / entree: A main dish ordered as part of a meal from the menu-items group, not permission to enter; show the plated main course.
polysemy_resolution_table.grate: The food-preparation verb of grating an ingredient on a grater, not a metal grille.
polysemy_resolution_table.mash: The food-preparation verb of crushing cooked food with a masher, not the hospital acronym.
polysemy_resolution_table.slice: The food-preparation verb of cutting a thin piece, not the portion or spatula noun.
polysemy_resolution_table.side: The side/accompaniment course in the meal group, not a geometric face; pair it with a main dish when useful.
polysemy_resolution_table.check (restaurant): The restaurant bill/check from the ordering and payment group, not a checkmark or obstacle.
polysemy_resolution_table.order: Placing a restaurant food order, not command or sequence.
polysemy_resolution_table.tip: A gratuity left for service, not a pointed end.
polysemy_resolution_table.take out: Food ordered to be taken away in a container; illustrate the action/packed order, distinct from the noun takeout meal container.
polysemy_resolution_table.takeout: Prepared restaurant food packed for takeaway as the noun/concept, distinct from the act of taking out a specific order.

contrast_notes.café / restaurant / bar (pub) / food sta: Café is a compact coffee-and-pastry shop; restaurant has a seated dining room; pub bar has counter and beer taps; food stall is a small outdoor counter beneath a canopy.
contrast_notes.appetizer / main course / entrée / side: Use course scale and plate contents to separate starters, central entrée/main, smaller side, and sweet dessert.
contrast_notes.fixed menu / set menu / buffet / special: Fixed/set menu is a prearranged group of courses; buffet is a self-serve spread; specials are a small featured group shown apart from a regular menu.
contrast_notes.chop / cut / grate / mash / mince / peel: Show the tool, food and resulting shape: large chunks, clean cut, shreds, crushed mash, tiny mince, removed peel, thin slice.
contrast_notes.bake / boil / broil / fry / grill / poac: Use oven, water, overhead heat, pan oil, grill bars, gentle water cooking, dry oven roast, and low bubbling pot respectively.
contrast_notes.check / receipt / tip / service charge: Check is the itemized bill to review; receipt is proof after payment; tip is separate money for service; service charge is a fee included in the bill.
contrast_notes.pay separately / split the check: Pay separately shows distinct diners paying their own totals; split the check shows one shared bill divided among the party.
